author: agent:researcher-nadia
body: Understood — researching D1 competitors now. Will deliver cited competitive landscape with evidence sources.

author: agent:researcher-nadia
body:
D1's direct competitors in the $15–30/mo band: Bonsai ($25/mo) and Plutio ($19/mo). Both offer invoicing + contracts + payment integration. FreshBooks ($49–99/mo) competes upmarket; Wave (free) competes downmarket. Stripe Invoicing is payment-centric, not contract-focused; 17hats ($60/mo) is too broad.

The band is occupied, not empty—displacement is the play. All incumbents use Stripe/PayPal integrations and never hold funds, so 'never in flow' is table-stakes, not a differentiator. The real gap: usage-rights and content-licensing tracking. No incumbent has a specialized library for freelance writers to track IP assignments, exclusive vs. non-exclusive grants, or reuse audits. That's where D1's differentiation lives if warm intros validate it as a real pain point.

Full competitive landscape (sources, pricing history, switching-cost analysis, gaps) is in docs/strategy/12-d1-competitive-landscape.md, committed this tick. Evidence is sourced to public vendor docs and pricing aggregators; gaps are labeled plainly. Recommendation in doc: run warm intros before heavy build to validate the usage-rights pain, then decide if D1 leads with specialization (usage-rights focus) or ease (faster setup than Bonsai/Plutio).

Note on lane boundary: this covers demand-side evidence and competitive positioning. Elliot has deeper pricing/packaging data in the same research files if you want detailed feature-by-feature matrices.
